restrictions: Messages M(x) = 0^32 || LE32(x) for a 256-bit point x: one 64-byte chunk of one block, root compression with IV, counter 0, block length 64, flags 11, rounds 0..2; f(x) = the complete 256-bit digest. Distinct points with equal f give two distinct messages with equal complete digests (proof.md Section 2).

Distinguished-point parallel collision search (van Oorschot-Wiener) on g(x) = f(x) XOR q (q a fixed mask, the digest-plane polarity) with 256 trails per batch: d = 114, cap 9 L, starts R + i from one random word R, a table of 23,000 entries of 32 bytes, one recovery with the selected-round compression, B = 1361685196381096540991432597423271205 batches (proof.md Section 5).

Each batch evaluates g on 256 trails with a generated bit-sliced straight line of 17,355 register operations (14,265 XOR, 1,030 AND, 2,060 OR): rotations renamed, constants and NOT folded into plane polarities, every full adder built around the input of different polarity (five operations a bit); checked against the plain three-round compression and run by the organizer experiments (proof.md Section 3).

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5, unit 638: N = 23943506716316778410370722130063836083099 word operations including recovery compression calls at 638 each, every handler bounded; time_log2 = 124.81935 is log2(N/638) rounded up, by the integer certificate of proof.md Section 6.3.

Machine convention H_reg: a declared file of 1,024 registers of 256 bits (peak use 771), its 32,768 bytes counted as memory; the main loop has no loads or stores. Priced alternatives: 512 registers +0.0907, 256 +0.2731, 64 +0.6160 (proof.md Section 10).

Memory at most 1,036,023 bytes <= 2^20 (straight line 5 bytes per instruction, other code 40 bytes per instruction, registers, lane state, scratch, table), so normalizedTimeMemoryLog2 = time_log2 (proof.md Section 4.3). Preprocessing is the generation of the straight line, charged 2^32 operations. No advice.

Success at least 0.3905 for one attempt over the fresh word R, under the score-critical premise H_rand that g behaves as a random function on the evaluated points; the bound subtracts unfinished and cut trails, table overflow, key false matches, Robin Hood starts and the stage-1 halt (proof.md Section 7). No full-scale run and no collision are claimed.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's fresh coins (the random word R that fixes the starts R + i), the images under g(x) = f(x) XOR q of the points the search evaluates behave as those of a uniformly random function from 256-bit values to 256-bit values: conditioned on the history of the attempt, the image of a point not evaluated before is uniform and independent of the earlier images. With it, the probability that the at least M = Q - 480 L points of finished trails contain no two distinct points with equal images is at most exp(-M(M-1)/2^257) = 0.6094898 (proof.md Section 7.4), and the success probability is at least 0.3905.
heuristics.scope: The three-round chain g on the points of one attempt: about 2^128.03 evaluations along trails of mean length 2^114 from starts R + i, i < 2^15. Only the pair-collision rate among evaluated images and the distinguished-point rate (density 2^-114 on fixed low bits) enter the bound; trail lengths enter through the geometric law of the distance to a distinguished point.
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer-executed evidence on the target with the shipped straight line: rho-w22 runs the claimed search end to end at width 22 (expected about 136.9 of 256 successes if the 22-bit chain behaves as a random function, from an ideal-function control of 4,000 attempts at the same parameters; our 1,500 target attempts gave 0.559); proj-w256 runs eight chained full-width steps from random planes and tests 22-bit image agreements among 2,048 iterates (expected 100.7 of 256). The organizer recomputes every returned pair. Extrapolated from 22-bit projections and 3,584 evaluations per trial to the full 256-bit images and 2^128 evaluations.
heuristics.limitations: A premise about one fixed function; no proof is known and it cannot be tested at width 256. The experiments reach 22-bit projections and chains of at most a few thousand points per trial; the full functional graph, trails of length 2^114 and the 256-bit collision rate are not measured. The bound tolerates a pair-collision deficit eps up to 0.0016; a larger deficit costs 0.5 log2(1/(1-eps)) bits (proof.md Section 8).

heuristics.statement: Machine convention: the 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5 with a declared file of 1,024 registers; operations on register operands cost one word operation each and need no load or store, and the 32,768 bytes of the file are counted in memory. The cost model fixes no register count.
heuristics.scope: The main-loop straight line (17,355 operations per batch, inputs and digests in registers 0 to 255, temporaries in 256 to 1,023, peak 771). Handlers, the recovery and the setup count their loads and stores.
heuristics.extrapolation: None statistical: it is a declared convention. Its price is computed with the same straight line and Belady allocation: 512 registers add 1,128 loads and stores per batch (+0.0907 bit), 256 registers 3,624 (+0.2731), 64 registers 9,263 (+0.6160), proof.md Section 10.
heuristics.limitations: If a reviewer requires a smaller register file the cost rises by the priced amount (124.91005 with 512 registers, 125.09245 with 256, 125.43535 with 64); the success argument is unaffected.
